summary: Chad's immigration directorate says that from 11 May 2026 every new visa application must be submitted through the online platform evisa.td, and that after 21 May 2026 a visa issued outside the platform is invalid and does not allow entry. The platform says nationals of the countries on its exemption list are exempt from visas, and the CEMAC Additional Act of 25 June 2013 gives nationals of CEMAC member states the right to travel without a visa and stay up to 90 days in another member state. The UK government advises against all travel to the northern provinces, western Kanem, the Lake Chad region and within 30 km of Chad's other borders, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Chad.

Chad's immigration directorate says that after 21 May 2026 a visa issued outside evisa.td is invalid. The platform says you cannot apply more than 90 days before your date of entry, recommends applying at least seven days ahead, says refunds are not possible and that an e-Visa cannot be modified once issued.

The UK government says that if you stay in Chad more than 72 hours you must register with the police at the Commissariat Central (police headquarters) on Avenue General Kerim Nassour, and that you must bring a passport photograph.

The Government of Canada says you are required to have a government permit for all photography in Chad, that it is prohibited to photograph airports, military establishments and government buildings, and that film and cameras may be confiscated without notice.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Chad?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you are exempt. Chad's e-Visa platform says nationals of the countries on its list are exempt from visas: Barbados, Benin, Bermuda, Congo, Dominica, Gabon, Gambia, Equatorial Guinea, the Cook Islands, Malaysia, Mali, Micronesia, Niger, Nigeria, the Central African Republic, Rwanda, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Singapore, Suriname and Togo. The CEMAC Additional Act of 25 June 2013 gives nationals of CEMAC member states the right to travel without a visa and stay up to 90 days in another member state. The platform lets any foreigner who is not exempt from a visa submit an e-Visa application online.

faq.question: Does Chad have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes. Chad's immigration directorate says all visa applications are now made exclusively online through evisa.td: from 11 May 2026 every new application must go through the platform (diplomatic and courtesy visas excepted), and after 21 May 2026 a visa issued outside it is invalid and does not allow entry. The platform recommends applying at least seven days before your date of entry and says you cannot apply more than 90 days before it. The directorate refers to a new fee grid; no official source we could read publishes the amounts.

faq.question: Is Chad safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK government advises against all travel to the northern provinces (Borkou, Ennedi Ouest, Ennedi Est and Tibesti), the western part of Kanem Province including Nokou, the Lake Chad region and within 30 km of all Chad's other borders, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Chad, including N'Djamena.

faq.question: Do I have to register after arriving in Chad?
faq.answer: Yes — the UK government says that if you stay in Chad more than 72 hours you must register with the police, that the immigration officer will tell you to go to the Commissariat Central (police headquarters) on Avenue General Kerim Nassour, and that you must bring a passport photograph.
